{{Short description|Geometric group theory}}
In the mathematical subject of [[geometric group theory]], the '''Baumslag–Gersten group''', also known as the '''Baumslag group''', is a particular [[one-relator group]] exhibiting some remarkable properties regarding its finite [[quotient group]]s, its [[Dehn function]] and the complexity of its [[word problem for groups|word problem]].

The group is given by the [[group presentation|presentation]]

: <math> G=\langle a,t \mid a^{a^t}=a^2\rangle =\langle a, t \mid (t^{-1}a^{-1}t) a (t^{-1} at)=a^2 \rangle  </math>

Here exponential notation for group elements denotes conjugation, that is, <math>g^h=h^{-1}gh</math> for <math>g, h\in G</math>.

==History==
The Baumslag–Gersten group ''G'' was originally introduced in a 1969 paper of [[Gilbert Baumslag]],<ref name=B>{{cite journal|first=Gilbert |last=Baumslag|authorlink= Gilbert Baumslag|title=A non-cyclic one-relator group all of whose finite factor groups are cyclic|journal= [[Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society]] |volume=10|year= 1969|pages= 497–498|mr=0254127 |doi=10.1017/S1446788700007783|doi-access=free}}</ref> as an example of a non-[[residually finite]] [[one-relator group]] with an additional remarkable property that all finite [[quotient group]]s of this group are cyclic. Later, in 1992, [[Stephen M. Gersten|Stephen Gersten]]<ref name=Ger>{{citation|first=Stephen M.|last= Gersten|authorlink= Stephen M. Gersten|contribution=Dehn functions and <math>l_1</math>-norms of finite presentations|title= Algorithms and classification in combinatorial group theory (Berkeley, CA, 1989)|pages= 195–224|series= Math. Sci. Res. Inst. Publ.|volume= 23|publisher= Springer|location= New York|year= 1992|doi=10.1007/978-1-4613-9730-4_9|mr=1230635}} </ref> showed that ''G'', despite being a one-relator group given by a rather simple presentation, has the [[Dehn function]] growing very quickly, namely faster than any fixed iterate of the exponential function. This example remains the fastest known growth of the Dehn function among one-relator groups. In 2011 Alexei Myasnikov, Alexander Ushakov, and Dong Wook Won<ref name="MUW">{{cite journal|first1=Alexei|last1= Myasnikov|first2= Alexander|last2= Ushakov|first3= Dong Wook|last3= Won|title=The word problem in the Baumslag group with a non-elementary Dehn function is polynomial time decidable|journal=[[Journal of Algebra]] |volume=345|year=2011|pages= 324–342| doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2011.07.024|arxiv= 1102.2481|mr=2842068}}</ref> proved that ''G'' has the [[word problem for groups|word problem]] solvable in polynomial time.

==Baumslag-Gersten group as an HNN extension==

The Baumslag–Gersten group ''G'' can also be realized as an [[HNN extension]] of the [[Baumslag–Solitar group]] <math>BS(1,2)=\langle a, b\mid a^b=a^2\rangle </math> with stable letter ''t'' and two cyclic associated subgroups<math>\langle a\rangle, \langle b\rangle </math>:

:<math>G=\langle a,t \mid a^{a^t}=a^2\rangle=\langle a,b,t \mid a^b=a^2, a^t=b\rangle.  </math>

==Properties of the Baumslag–Gersten group ''G''==

*Every finite [[quotient group]] of ''G'' is [[cyclic group|cyclic]]. In particular, the group ''G'' is not [[residually finite group|residually finite]].<ref name=B/>
*An endomorphism of ''G'' is either an automorphism or its image is a cyclic subgroup of ''G''. In particular the group ''G'' is [[Hopfian group|Hopfian]] and [[co-Hopfian group|co-Hopfian]].<ref name=Br>
{{cite journal
| last       = Brunner
| first      = Andrew
| date       = 1980
| title      = On a class of one-relator groups
| jstor        = 
| journal    = [[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]] 
| mr         = 571934
| volume     = 32
| issue      = 2
| pages      = 414–420
| doi        = 10.4153/CJM-1980-032-8
| doi-access= free
}}
</ref>  
*The [[outer automorphism group]] Out(''G'') of ''G'' is isomorphic to the additive group of dyadic rationals <math>\mathbb Z\left[\frac{1}{2}\right]</math> and in particular is not finitely generated.<ref name=Br/> 
*Gersten proved<ref name=Ger/> that the [[Dehn function]] ''f''(''n'') of ''G'' grows faster than any fixed iterate of the exponential. Subsequently A. N. Platonov<ref>{{cite journal |first=A.N. |last=Platonov |title=An isoparametric function of the Baumslag–Gersten group |journal=Moscow Univ. Math. Bull. |volume=59 |issue=3 |pages=12–17 |year=2004 |mr=2127449 |url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/eng/vmumm1241 }}</ref> proved that ''f(n)'' is equivalent to 

:: <math> \exp^{\circ\log n}(1)=(\exp\underbrace{\circ \cdots  \circ}_{\log n \text{ times } } \exp)(1) </math>

*Myasnikov, Ushakov, and Won,<ref name=MUW/> using compression methods of "power circuits" arithmetics, proved that the word problem in ''G'' is solvable in polynomial time. Thus the group ''G'' exhibits a large gap between the growth of its Dehn function and the complexity of its word problem.
* The [[conjugacy problem]] in ''G'' is known to be decidable, but the only known worst-case upper bound estimate for the complexity of the conjugacy problem, due to Jannis Beese, is [[Elementary function arithmetic|elementary recursive]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Beese |first=Jannis |date=2012 |title=Das Konjugations problem in der Baumslag–Gersten–Gruppe |type=Diploma |publisher=Fakultät Mathematik, Universität Stuttgart }}</ref> It is conjectured that this estimate is sharp, based on some reductions to power circuit division problems.<ref name=DMW>{{cite journal |first=Volker |last=Diekert |first2=Alexei G. |last2=Myasnikov |first3=Armin  |last3=Weiß |title=Conjugacy in Baumslag's group, generic case complexity, and division in power circuits |journal=Algorithmica |volume=76 |issue=4 |pages=961–988 |year=2016 |doi=10.1007/s00453-016-0117-z |mr=3567623|arxiv=1309.5314 }}</ref> There is a [[generic-case complexity|strongly generically]] polynomial time solution of the conjugacy problem for ''G''.<ref name=DMW/>

==Generalizations==

*Andrew Brunner<ref name=Br/> considered one-relator groups of the form
:: <math>\langle a,t\mid (a^p)^{(t^{-1}a^kt)}=a^m \rangle, </math> where <math>p,k,m\ne 0</math>
and generalized many of Baumslag's original results in that context.
*[[Mahan Mitra]]<ref>{{cite journal |authorlink=Mahan Mitra |first=Mahan |last=Mitra |title=Coarse extrinsic geometry: a survey |journal=Geom. Topol. Monogr. |volume=1 |pages=341–364 |year=1998 |doi=10.2140/gtm.1998.1.341 |mr=1668308 |arxiv=math.DG/9810203|series=Geometry & Topology Monographs }}</ref> considered a [[word-hyperbolic group|word-hyperbolic]] analog ''G'' of the Baumslag–Gersten group, where Mitra's group possesses a rank three free subgroup that is highly distorted in ''G'', namely where the subgroup distortion is higher than any fixed iterated power of the exponential.
